title: New <graph> tag

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
## New element proposal

Hi, I'm Oren Lavie, an eleven-year-old beginner developer. In my time learning HTML, I noticed that there is no HTML-native way to make equation-based graphs without JS or any dependencies. I decided to come up with a `<graph>` tag with the following attributes:

width (in px, but you don't need to write "px" as a whole), default 0
height (also in px), default 0
alt (for screen readers)
equation (for the actual graph to begin with) default "x^2"
fill (can be an HTML named color, hex code, rgb, hsl, rgba, hsla), default black
offsetx, offsety (bottom-left corner is the point (offsetx, offsety)), default 0
zoom (zoom: the scale becomes 1/the number specified), default 1

and attributes that don't need a value:

nogridx
nogridy
noxline
noyline
noxnums
noynums
panning
zoomwheel

Equation format:

equation="x^2"

The goal is to have a sort of built-in Desmos, with many scientific functions and calculus.

For derivatives and integrals:

deriv(x^3)
int(lower, upper, function)

For multiple graphs in one:

`<gc>
           <graph equation="x+1" fill="red">
           <graph equation="sqrt(x)" fill="blue">
</gc>`

EXAMPLE:

`<gc>
<graph equation="2x+1" fill="green" alt="The graph of two x plus one">
<graph equation="sqrt(sin(x))" fill="#f0f0f0>
</gc>`
